topics.definition: A Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) processes sequential data by using information from previous time steps.
RNNs maintain a hidden state that carries information through a sequence.
tips: Simple RNNs struggle with long sequences.

topics.definition: Gradients can become extremely small during training, making it difficult to learn long-term dependencies.
tips: LSTM and GRU help solve this issue.

topics.definition: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks use gates to remember and forget information over long sequences.
topics.syntax: Input Gate + Forget Gate + Output Gate

topics.definition: Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) simplify LSTM while retaining strong performance.
Sequence modeling predicts or analyzes ordered data.
RNNs, LSTMs and GRUs are used for translation, text generation, speech recognition and sentiment analysis.
tips: Transformers are now common for many NLP tasks.

topics.definition: Choose the architecture based on sequence length, monitor training and prevent overfitting.
